transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-17
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Daniel Reyes (CTO, Nexa), Maya Singh (ML Eng, Nexa), Oliver Park (Infra, Nexa)
Recording note: mobile mic on for a few minutes, minor dropouts

Summary:
Redwood and Nexa reviewed the latest POC weekly benchmark results comparing Redwood's hosted/dedicated configs vs the customer's baseline provider (VendorX/CloudProvider). Discussion focused on latency (p99/p50), throughput (tokens/sec & requests/sec), batching behavior, quantization effects, and infrastructure differences (GPU types, sequence lengths). Action items agreed for sharing detailed CSVs, scheduling an infra profiling session, and sending security docs/pricing.

Topics:
- Baseline vs Redwood numbers (latency/throughput)
- Hotspots: KV cache warmup, batch sizing, quantization tradeoffs
- Network/VPC considerations for private deployment
- Next steps: deeper profiling, sample load script, pricing & sizing

00:00 Liam: "Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — Liam from Redwood here, Priya's with me. Nexa folks?"
00:08 Daniel: "Hi, Daniel here, Maya and Oliver with me, thanks Liam."
00:15 Priya: "Cool, so today we'll walk through the bench spreadsheet we dropped earlier — main focus p99 latency and steady-state throughput vs your baseline provider."
00:30 Maya: "Yep we pulled the numbers this morning. Quick note: we ran sequences at 512 tokens and 1024 for longer context tests, like we discussed."
00:44 Priya: "Right — I have the slide that sums p50/p90/p99 across models: tiny-distil, med-7b, large-13b quantized. For med-7b on Redwood Hosted we see median ttr around 60ms, p99 ~220ms, throughput about 14 rps under the current workload. Baseline provider shows p99 around 380ms and throughput 9 rps."
01:12 Daniel: "Wait — that's a pretty big gap, are you running batching the same way? Our baseline uses their managed batching which is opaque to us, we tried match config as much as possible."
01:25 Priya: "We matched request patterns and concurrency; we also ran a separate test with explicit batching (batch size 8) and auto-batching off. When we did that Redwood throughput increased to 20 rps, p99 dropped to 180ms. So batching helps a lot."
01:56 Oliver: "Question about GPU types — what's running on Redwood? Because baseline is on A100s, we thought they'd have the edge."
02:06 Liam: "We're on an optimized fleet: a mix of A100 and H100 depending on the cluster. For these tests we pegged to H100 equivalent nodes for med-7b, but one confounder is our quantization path. We used int8 streaming for 13b which reduced mem pressure."
02:34 Maya: "I noticed in the CSV there's a warmup period where p99 spikes — is that K V cache warming?"
02:40 Priya: "Yep that's the K V cache warmup, and also initial kernel selection. We see spikes for first few minutes; steady-state after cache warm is much lower. You can see that in the per-minute chart we uploaded."
03:05 Daniel: "Baseline provider also had a warmup but it was longer — maybe they don't do prefix caching in the same way."
03:17 Priya: "Correct, their architecture seems to favor cold-start isolation which adds tail latency. Our smart routing and prefix cache reduces that for repeat contexts."
03:40 Oliver: "Network wise — for private deployment we need to test VPC peering. Did the hosted tests include any extra egress latency?"
03:48 Liam: "Hosted tests were run from our us-west region and the test runner was in the same region, so egress minimal. For private, once peered, we expect <5ms added H2S for your region, but we'll confirm in the profiling run."
04:10 Maya: "On quantization — the 13b int8 numbers look much better on throughput, but quality regression on some of our evaluations popped up — is that expected?"
04:20 Priya: "There is a small accuracy delta; our Optimize tool suggested mixed quantization for your prompt set (int8 on attention + fp16 residuals), that keeps quality closer to baseline with big perf wins. We can share the per-prompt drop table."
04:42 Daniel: "Can you explain the p99 measurement — is it server-side only or includes network? We need to ensure apples-to-apples."
04:51 Priya: "We measured end-to-end from the runner (so includes network between tester and endpoint). In the spreadsheet there's a server-only column (internal trace) — server-only p99 was about 180ms for med-7b on Redwood Hosted."
05:18 Maya: "We've got a few longer tail queries in our workload which inflate p99. Would you recommend per-route timeouts or separate route for long-horizon generation?"
05:28 Liam: "Yes — recommended to SLO-split by route: low-latency routes go to the low-latency pool (smaller seq, pinned model), long-horizon to a high-throughput pool. We can map those in a follow-up doc."
05:45 Priya: "Also autoscaling configs — for this POC we set a conservative scale-up threshold. If you bump it aggressive you'll see improved p99 at cost tradeoff."
06:02 Daniel: "About cost — rough delta vs baseline? We need to see per-token unit cost and reserved vs on-demand."
06:10 Liam: "I'll send a pricing delta spreadsheet; short answer: at the throughput levels you're testing Hosted is slightly higher per-token than baseline but Dedicated reserved capacity crosses a threshold where Redwood is cheaper overall due to better packing and prefix cache. I'll include example commit sizes."
06:30 Oliver: "Is Dedicated the recommended path for production?"
06:34 Priya: "For consistent high throughput and strict data isolation, yes. Hosted is fine for initial rollouts and can be cheaper at low volume. Dedicated gives predictable latency and can be network-isolated (VPC)."
06:48 Daniel: "Security wise: can you confirm SOC2, SAML, and KMS options? We have to satisfy audit."
06:55 Liam: "Yes — SOC2 in place, SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC supported, and KMS/HSM integration for private deployments. We'll send the SOC2 whitepaper and the SSO guide after the call."
07:12 Maya: "One more thing — the baseline used mixed CPU/GPU offload for long sequences; does Redwood support that fallback?"
07:20 Priya: "We recommend GPU-first for latency-critical, but we have offload options in private deployments. There's also a quantization and kernel path we can tune for long sequences."
07:34 Daniel: "OK let's walk the specific numbers: can you open the med-7b sheet?"
07:40 Priya: "Pulling it up — paginating to relevant table. med-7b, seq512, concurrency 16: Redwood Hosted p50 60ms, p90 120ms, p99 220ms, throughput 14 rps. Baseline p50 110ms, p90 260ms, p99 380ms, throughput 9 rps. Dedicated numbers (Redwood) show p99 ~160ms, throughput 18 rps at similar load because of pinned GPUs and higher packing efficiency."
08:18 Daniel: "Those Dedicated numbers look compelling. How reproducible are they in our environment?"
08:25 Priya: "Reasonably reproducible — but two things: your test runner region and VPC peering matter; also sequence length distribution matters a lot. We'll run a profiling session inside your VPC to validate."
08:40 Oliver: "We'll need a testing window next week; we can open a test subnet. ETA for credentials?"
08:47 Daniel: "I'll get the infra team to open a window, Oliver will coordinate. Targeting Nov 24 as discussed."
08:55 Maya: "About the CSV — there's a column called "unified_kv_miss" — can you explain?"
09:02 Priya: "That's a metric for K V cache misses when you route by prefix; high miss means less cache benefit for repeated contexts, often seen with low reuse patterns."
09:18 Daniel: "On the quality side with int8, can you run the eval suite we shared and produce diff summary?"
09:25 Priya: "Yes we'll run the evals against mixed-quant and full-fp16 and give a per-prompt delta table. Expect that by 2026-11-19."
09:40 Liam: "Couple of operational notes: we'll include runbooks for canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to baseline provider if Dedicated capacity is saturated. That was one of your asks earlier, right?"
09:50 Daniel: "Yes failover is required — we want automatic fallback to baseline if capacity hits 95% and degrade smartly."
10:00 Priya: "We can configure policy: route first to Dedicated, fallback to Hosted or Baseline depending on cost/latency policy. We'll include recommended policy configs."
10:16 Oliver: "One more infra detail — will logs/audit show per-token traces or just request-level meta?"
10:22 Liam: "We can surface token-level breakdowns for debugging in Sandbox, but for production we'd typically surface request-level with cost/latency aggregates; token-level is available behind consent and retained per retention policy."
10:38 Maya: "Any notable regressions vs baseline in terms of hallucinations or coherence on long prompts? We saw some divergence at 1024 tokens."
10:45 Priya: "Slight divergence on a small subset; it correlates with quantization and kernel selection. Our Optimize recommendations include prompt-specific tuning and sometimes switching architecture variant for long-horizon prompts."
11:05 Daniel: "Ok let's line up owners: Priya runs the profiling and shares per-model CSVs; Liam sends pricing and security docs; Nexa provides load script and opens test window."
11:12 Liam: "Yep — I'll follow up with links: Benchmark Spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/nexa-2026-11 (internal link), SOC2 + SSO: https://redwood.app/security/nexa-pack, Pricing delta sheet: attached in follow-up email."
11:30 Maya: "Anything else?"
11:33 Daniel: "No, thanks — this was helpful. We want the detailed CSVs and to confirm the Nov 24 profiling window."
11:40 Liam: "Great — will do. Thanks everyone."
